esērum: UNCERTAIN: to press, constrain (a debtor): isiršuma “he pressed him, and” (preterite + -šu + -ma); the sense is taken from context
-šum: to him, for him (dative suffix -šum, on a verb): ibaššišum “there is to him”, iqbišum “he said to him”, inaddiššum “he shall give him”
tarkibtum: UNCERTAIN: perhaps the putting in order of an orchard handed over (a noun, perhaps from rakābum “to mount”): ištu tarkibtim “after the putting in order (?)” (genitive); the sense is a guess from context
suluppû: dates, the date crop (a collective noun, treated as plural; two signs, read ZÚ.LUM today, KA.LUM in Ungnad’s reading): suluppî (oblique case); suluppî watrūtim “the surplus dates”
mala: as many as, as much as (introducing a relative clause): mala ina kirîm ibbaššû “as many as are in the orchard”
bašûm-N: N-stem of bašûm: to be there, be found: ibbaššû (present, 3rd plural, in a ša-clause) “which are found”
-ka: your (masc. sg.), possessive suffix on a noun: bītika “your house”, kaspika “your silver”, niditika / niditka “your vacant plot”, nabalkatka “your crossing-over (?)”
apālum: to answer; to satisfy, pay (a creditor): ippalma (present, with -ma) “he shall pay, and”
tēḫûm: UNCERTAIN: perhaps “adjoining piece, neighbouring plot” (Ungnad’s guess, his glossary hedged); tēḫûšu “the plot adjoining it (?)”
nabalkattum: UNCERTAIN: apparently “crossing-over”, a noun from the root BLKT of nabalkutum “to cross over”; nabalkatka “your crossing-over (?)”; the sense is a guess, and the word is broken in places (naba…, …katim)
šubalkutum: UNCERTAIN: Š-stem of the root BLKT (nabalkutum “to cross over”): “to make cross over”; ušbalakatūnim (present, 3rd plural, with ventive -nim) “they make (it) cross over (?)”; the sense is a guess
-kum: to you, for you (masc. sg.), dative suffix -kum; kum is the fragment of such an ending
kiṣrum: UNCERTAIN: rent, a tenant’s payment for a house (written KA.SAR, per Ungnad’s footnote): kasap kiṣri(šu) “the silver of (his) rent”; the sense is taken from context
malûm: to be full; malûtim (feminine plural adjective, genitive) “full”: lā malûtim “not full”, said of the days of a lease; malû… is a broken form

__broaden__.bašûm: to exist, arise: ibbaššû “which arose” · lā ibaššišum “there is not to him” (= he has none), with dative -šum
__broaden__.wašābum: to sit: ul uššab “he shall not sit” (the stone writes uš-ta-ab — a carver’s slip Harper flags) · to dwell: wāšbum (participle, contracted) “the dweller, the tenant” (a conjectured reading, aš-bu-u[m]); wa… “dwell-” in broken forms
__broaden__.epēšum: to do, make: epēšim “doing” · to work (land): ippeš(ma) (present): eqlam šipram ippeš “he shall do the work on the field” · to build (?) (a house): bītam ippēšma(?) “he builds a house, and”, the verb broken; iteppuš (?) in a broken line
__broaden__.watārum: to exceed; Š-stem — mušāter “who makes surpassing”; ušāterūšu “they made it supreme” · watrum “surplus, in excess”: watrūtim (feminine plural) said of the surplus dates
__broaden__.ūmum: day; ūmišu “daily” (written UD-mi-šu) · plural “days”: ūmī (written UD-mi-) “days”: ina ūmīšu lā malûtim “in his days not full” (the days of a lease)
